## Context / Problem

The principal-engineer Janitor audit at snapshot `9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301` verified maintainability, oracle, documentation, compatibility, and dead-code findings that passed the fixed validity and impact floors and were approved by the maintainer. The audit itself changed no product code; this epic delivers the approved cleanup before further feature work consumes the recovered headroom.

Authoritative evidence and dispositions are in `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md` and audit ticket `literal-subaverage-dartfrog`.

## Approach

Deliver each approved remediation through a non-overlapping child whose plan owns its cited files and regression contracts. Structural extractions follow existing call-graph seams. Public removals state their replacement and breaking-change impact. Internal-only shim removal is gated by a prerequisite ADR and migrates every static, dynamic, string, test, and monkeypatch consumer before deletion. Reconciler compatibility removal is separately dependency-ordered so persisted state and live lock/exit contracts are migrated before old routes disappear.

## Child Decomposition

- Structural-headroom children own RP01, RP07, and RP13.
- Behavioral-oracle and CI children own RP05, RP06, RP09, RP14, RP16, RP19, RP29, RP31, RP33, and RP36.
- Adapter and documentation children own RP10, RP20, RP21, RP22, RP23, RP24, RP28, and RP35.
- Public-deprecation and compatibility children own RP18, RP27, scheduled removals, config aliases, CLI aliases, the reconcile family, Python/MCP aliases, and MCP model re-exports.
- The internal-shim container owns the prerequisite ADR and disjoint implementation shards, including SDC3.
- Supplemental leaves own SDC1, SDC2, and SDC4.
- RP02 and RP03 were already absorbed into completed `financial-stoneware-brant` work and are not duplicated here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [RP01/S13] Fsck repair planning, policy, restoration, pause, and application are separated along existing call-graph seams while abort semantics remain covered.
- [x] [RP05/O02] The config-surface golden rejects every unregistered live schema key and canonical environment name.
- [x] [RP06/O14] A behavioral oracle proves an effectful workflow step is invoked once and serially when it raises.
- [x] [RP07/S04] Only the MCP startup-handshake cluster is extracted, with lifecycle ordering and compatibility seams unchanged.
- [x] [RP09/O12/O13] Tests parse the shipped Docker stage and prove the health command opens the configured socket and fails on a bad response without requiring Docker in the normal test path.
- [x] [RP10/A06] Jira Cloud and Data Center delegate link normalization to one pure Jira-family canonicalizer while transports and provider-neutral diffing remain separate.
- [x] [RP13/S11] Independent table-driven LLM configuration readers leave `LLMConfig.from_env` as the sole precedence facade.
- [x] [RP14/T07] Pinned deployed Semgrep and Gitleaks integrations run in a portable direct-binary parallel Verified lane.
- [x] [RP16/O11/O07/O10] Sidecar stores use conflict-safe read-merge-write and observational concurrency/durability proofs.
- [x] [RP18/A13] Caller-selected reviewer inputs are removed from CLI, Python, MCP, and generated contracts before any billable call.
- [x] [RP19/S05] Production mutation builders emit create/parent ordering metadata and planner/dispatcher tests prove the order.
- [x] [RP20/C01/C02/C04/D06] Reconciler rollout, arbitration, configuration, and rollback documentation matches verified runtime behavior.
- [x] [RP21/C11/C12] Canonical review/gate descriptions are corrected and the existing MCP reference regenerated.
- [x] [RP22/D01] Maintained CLI guidance no longer advertises the removed `review` route.
- [x] [RP23/D02] Ticket types and statuses are generated from the canonical schema with drift checking.
- [x] [RP24/D05] Bug guidance documents claim-time exemption followed by post-RCA plan review for complex remediation.
- [x] [RP27/A11] The expired `REBAR_HLC=0` rollback branch is removed while legacy-event reads and clock injection remain.
- [x] [RP28/A12] Residual maintained severity-threshold guidance is removed and no operational config surface remains.
- [x] [RP29/O01] API snapshots include normalized return annotations and detect return-only drift.
- [x] [RP31/T02] The AST-identical blame-autoderivation test duplicate is removed without losing distinct boundary coverage.
- [x] [RP33/S16] Every third-party action in the privileged reconciliation workflow is full-SHA pinned and covered by existing security checks.
- [x] [RP35/S15] Git-backed `module_size_trend` and `cap_change_events` metrics implement the structured unavailable contract.
- [x] [RP36/O09] Truthful-tally tests require exact nonempty success output and reject empty output.
- [x] Scheduled public deprecations are removed with custom OpenAI-compatible Chat endpoints preserved.
- [x] All eight approved environment/config aliases are removed and canonical replacements are documented.
- [x] Simple CLI aliases are removed in favor of their canonical `bridge`/identity commands.
- [x] The complete `reconcile` and `reconcile-check` family is migrated to canonical bridge functionality, including persisted-state handling, then removed.
- [x] Python/MCP operation aliases are removed with their canonical replacements and breaking-change records.
- [x] Private MCP model re-exports are removed without changing MCP schemas or wire payloads.
- [x] A merged ADR prohibits internal-only compatibility shims while preserving deliberate public, wire, event, and persisted-data contracts.
- [x] Every inventoried internal shim consumer is migrated to its canonical owner and the old name/path is absent.
- [x] [SDC1] Dead reconciler retry/result residue is removed without changing live drift, lock-loss, bridge-exit, store-guard, or persisted-state contracts.
- [x] [SDC2] Superseded LLM workflow helpers are removed after their behavioral tests move to live owners.
- [x] [SDC4] Dead Jira adapter helpers are removed while mapper/codec and raw-PUT contracts remain covered.
